title: Confiscation of vehicle in excise cases - how to get it released
p1:
Your vehicle can be seized even when you are not the person accused of an excise offence.

Many vehicle owners discover this only after their vehicle is taken away during an excise case.
p2: A common misconception is that seizure automatically means permanent loss. In reality, confiscation and release are separate issues. A vehicle owner may have legal remedies to seek interim release or challenge confiscation proceedings, depending on the facts of the case.
p3:
The key is acting quickly. Authorities generally examine factors like ownership, knowledge of the alleged offence, and whether the owner took reasonable precautions. Keeping ownership documents, responding to notices, and approaching the appropriate authority or court can make a significant difference.

A seized vehicle is not always a lost vehicle. Timely legal action can protect valuable assets while the case continues.
